sections.label: Ownership and control approval
sections.summary: Changes in ownership or control that let a person direct regulated persons require IMDA's prior approval, including 30% interest, effective control or takeover.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Under the amended framework, changes in ownership or control that can allow any person to direct the actions of regulated persons will require IMDA’s prior approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Specifically, this would apply where a person acquires 30% or more interest in a regulated person, obtains effective control over its operations, or takes over its media business as a going concern.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: The 30% threshold in the Bill serves as a benchmark for when someone would presumably have control over the entity’s decisions and operations.

sections.label: IMDA directions for market conduct
sections.summary: Clause 6 empowers IMDA to issue directions to maintain fair and efficient market conduct or safeguard consumers' interests in media services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill empowers IMDA to issue directions for the purposes of maintaining fair and efficient market conduct or to safeguard consumers' interests by promoting fair, transparent and reliable provision of media services.

sections.label: Quick targeted media actions
sections.summary: The amendment lets IMDA take similar quick and targeted actions for the media sector through the issuance of directions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: With this amendment, IMDA can take similar quick and targeted actions for the media sector through the issuance of directions.

sections.label: Structural separation power to Minister
sections.summary: Clause 15 vests the power to order structural separation of a regulated person in the Minister rather than IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Second, clause 15 provides that the powers to order structural separation of a regulated person is vested in the Minister rather than IMDA.

sections.label: Updated regulated persons definition
sections.summary: Clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons to address potential gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Third, clause 3 updates the definition of parties who can be designated as regulated persons to address potential gaps.

sections.label: Approving external codes of practice
sections.summary: Clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister of Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Fourth, clause 5 allows IMDA to approve documents prepared by a person other than IMDA as a code of practice or standard of performance for the media sector.

sections.label: IMDA powers expansion in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill expands IMDA's toolkit with pre-emptive directions, tighter ownership controls and last-resort market restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: When regulatory powers become broader, the guardrails must become clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces a significant expansion of IMDA's toolkit, pre-emptive directions, tighter ownership controls and even the ability, as a last resort, to restructure parts of the market.

sections.label: IMDA early action and ownership
sections.summary: Under the Bill, IMDA can act before harm occurs or reshape ownership structures where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, IMDA can act before harm occurs or even reshape ownership structures, where necessary.

sections.label: Balancing three concerns, editorial decisions
sections.summary: The challenge is balancing all three carefully, and the Bill is not about influencing editorial decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The challenge is not choosing one over the other but balancing all three carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill is definitely not about influencing editorial decisions.

sections.label: Disciplined application of Bill powers
sections.summary: Over-intervention can reduce incentives to invest or innovate, so the Bill's powers must be applied in a disciplined, evidence-based and calibrated way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But over-intervention can sometimes reduce incentives to invest or innovate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Therefore, while the powers in the Bill are necessary, their application must be disciplined, evidence-based and carefully calibrated.

sections.label: Control and association definitions risk
sections.summary: Sections 59, 60A and 60B define control and association broadly, risking over-capture of legitimate business relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under sections 59, 60A and 60B, the definitions of control and association are broad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: However, there is also a risk that these definitions may over-capture legitimate business relationships, for example, a venture capital firm investing in multiple media companies or a strategic partnership by multiple firms without the intent to control or a collaborative ecosystem that supports innovation.

sections.label: Structural separation as last resort
sections.summary: Under section 69A, the Minister may order structural separation, which must remain a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under section 69A, the Minister may order structural separation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is one of the most powerful tools in the Bill and it must remain exactly what it was intended to be – a last resort.

sections.label: Separation order power to Minister
sections.summary: Clause 15 vests the power to issue separation orders directly in the Minister rather than IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One change in the Bill is clause 15, which amends the law to vest the power to issue a separation order, which can require a company to restructure or divest parts of its business to address competition concerns, directly in the Minister rather than IMDA.

sections.label: Dual track appeal mechanism
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a dual track appeal mechanism allowing affected parties to seek reconsideration or appeal to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill introduces a dual track appeal mechanism, allowing affected parties to seek reconsideration by the authority or appeal to the Minister.

sections.label: Expanded merger controls and media investment
sections.summary: Clause 3 expands merger controls to any person acquiring a 30% stake, prompting a question on blocking legitimate media investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the expansion of merger controls to any person acquiring a 30% stake in clause 3 gives the Government a virtual veto over the financing of media entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How will the Government reassure Singaporeans that the expanded merger controls will not be used to block legitimate investment in independent or alternative media platforms?

sections.label: Strengthening competition and media framework
sections.summary: The step is necessary to strengthen competition, align the media framework with telecommunications and equip IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is a vulnerability to our social resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is a necessary step to strengthen competition, align our media framework with the telecommunications sector and equip IMDA with the tools to act when markets do not function well.

sections.label: IMDA directions for market conduct
sections.summary: Under section 61A, IMDA may issue directions to ensure fair and efficient market conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 61A, IMDA may issue directions to ensure fair and efficient market conduct.

sections.label: IMDA powers over share disposal
sections.summary: Under section 65A, IMDA has powers to require disposal of shares or relinquishment of control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, under section 65A, IMDA has powers to require the disposal of shares or the relinquishment of control.

sections.label: Separation order transfers business
sections.summary: Section 69A allows a separation order to require transferring business to another entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under section 69A, a separation order may require the transfer of business to another entity.

sections.label: IMDA information powers and definitions
sections.summary: Passage asks how IMDA will avoid capturing ordinary collaborations, notes expanded regulated persons, and cites sections 65B and 71A information powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, given that they include arrangements and coordinated actions, can the Minister clarify how IMDA will ensure that ordinary commercial collaborations, especially among smaller players, are not inadvertently captured?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also note that the definition of regulated persons has been expanded to close potential gaps, including for entities structured through trusts or other arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Further, under sections 65B and 71A, IMDA is empowered to require information from any person for investigative purposes.

sections.label: Bill powers and compliance burden
sections.summary: Passage states the Bill reduces burden for some pro-forma transactions but expands investigative powers, and notes IMDA may approve third-party Codes of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the Bill reduces burden for certain pro-forma transactions, it also expands investigative and compliance powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If regulation becomes too complex, it risks disproportionately favouring larger players with greater compliance resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also note that IMDA may approve documents prepared by third parties as Codes of Practice.

sections.label: Three new Bill powers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a proactive directions regime under section 61A, an ownership approval regime under section 65, and a Ministerial separation order under section 69A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces three significant new powers: a proactive directions regime under the new section 61A, an ownership approval regime under the new section 65 and the Ministerial separation order under new section 69A.

sections.label: Minister designates regulated persons
sections.summary: The Minister can designate any newspaper publisher or broadcaster as a regulated person on no published criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister can designate any newspaper publisher or broadcaster as a "regulated person" on no published criteria and bring the full weight of this regime to bear.

sections.label: Jom investor approval and directions
sections.summary: An investor acquiring 30% or more of Jom needs IMDA's prior approval, and IMDA could issue proactive directions on undefined public interest grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any investor acquiring 30% or more of Jom would need IMDA's prior approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: IMDA could issue proactive directions to Jom on "public interest" grounds left undefined in the statute, with no proportionality test and consultation waivable at IMDA's discretion.

sections.label: IMDA approval for media acquisitions
sections.summary: Any person acquiring 30% or more of a regulated media company now requires IMDA's prior approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any person acquiring 30% or more of a regulated media company now requires IMDA's prior approval.

sections.label: Separation order and investment chilling effect
sections.summary: The passage states the chilling effect on investment in small independent publications is not incidental, and describes the section 69 separation order letting the Minister compel transfer of a media company's entire business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The chilling effect on investment in small, independent publications is not incidental to this drafting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And finally, the "nuclear" option, a separation order in section 69.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister may compel a media company to transfer its entire business to another entity.

sections.label: IMDA 2022 consultation on separation
sections.summary: IMDA's 2022 consultation note stated structural separation requirements may impose significant costs and should only be exercised in very exceptional circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: IMDA acknowledged the weight of this in its own 2022 consultation note.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It stated that structural separation requirements may impose significant costs and should only be exercised in very exceptional circumstances.

sections.label: Permit criteria after separation order
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to confirm a permit will not be withheld from an already separated entity and asks about published criteria for refusing a post-separation permit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that a permit will not be withheld from an entity that has already been compulsorily separated under Ministerial Order, and will there be published criteria governing when the permit application following separation may be refused?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That day has not come, but the conditions that will make it possible are things that Singapore can build.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It will only happen if we make deliberate choices to build safeguards into our legislative architecture and not simply rely on the goodwill of whoever holds office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That is why I hope that the Senior Minister of State can give us reassurance today that this Bill is intended to build regulatory architecture for the press that is designed to make a future of independent trusted journalism more reachable and not to close it off before it has the chance to arrive.

sections.label: Support for 30% threshold extension
sections.summary: The speaker supports extending IMDA's prior approval requirement to any acquisition crossing the 30% threshold in regulated media entities, including non-licensees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): I support the extension of IMDAs prior approval requirement to any acquisition crossing the 30% threshold in regulated media entities, including non-licensees.

sections.label: Distinguishing investment and concentration risk
sections.summary: The passage asks how IMDA will distinguish between capability-enhancing investment, competitive concentration risk and longer-term dependency creation within the ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The key implementation question is this: how will IMDA distinguish between capability-enhancing investment, competitive concentration risk and longer-term dependency creation within the ecosystem?

sections.label: Structural separation guiding principles
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will set out broad guiding principles on when structural separation is considered appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry set out broad guiding principles on when structural separation is considered appropriate?

sections.label: Illustrative guidance on material influence
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider issuing illustrative guidance with examples of material influence and essential resources in a converged media ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider issuing illustrative guidance, not fixed thresholds, but examples of what constitutes material influence in practice and what types of infrastructure or systems may be treated as essential resources in a converged media ecosystem?

sections.label: Bill strengthens media market conduct
sections.summary: States the Bill strengthens fair and efficient market conduct and competition, reduces regulatory burden, gives IMDA additional powers and aligns provisions with the Telecommunications Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That balance between firmness and legibility is what this Bill begins to strengthen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill strengthens fair and efficient market conduct and effective competition in the media industry, reduces regulatory burden in prescribed areas, provides IMDA with additional powers and align certain provisions with the Telecommunications Act.

sections.label: Consistent telecoms and media regulation
sections.summary: Asks how IMDA will ensure consistent principles across telecommunications and media competition regulation while accounting for the media sector's public interest considerations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In this regard, can the Minister clarify how IMDA will ensure consistent principles across telecommunications and media competition regulation while still accounting for the media sector's distinct public interest considerations?

sections.label: IMDA stronger intervention tools
sections.summary: States the Bill gives IMDA stronger tools to intervene on market conduct and essential resources in the media industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Bill gives IMDA stronger tools to intervene in relation to market conduct and essential resources in the media industry.

sections.label: Safeguards for market conduct directions
sections.summary: Asks what procedural safeguards, such as notice, representations and review avenues, will apply to the new power to issue directions for fair and efficient market conduct.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: On the new power to issue directions for fair and efficient market conduct, can the Senior Minister of State clarify what procedural safeguards will apply where practicable, such as notice, representations and review avenues, so that speed is balanced with due process?

sections.label: IMDA approval for media stakes
sections.summary: The Bill requires IMDA's prior approval before any party acquires a 30% or larger stake in a regulated media company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, IMDA must give prior approval before any party acquires a 30% or larger stake in a regulated media company.

sections.label: MOM 2025 labour market report
sections.summary: MOM's 2025 Labour Market Report listed information and communications among sectors where resident employment declined in 2025, while the economy grew over 5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: MOM’s Labour Market Report for 2025 identified information and communications as one of the sectors where resident employment declined in 2025, even as Singapore’s economy grew more than 5%.

sections.label: Workforce impact and tripartite questions
sections.summary: The passage asks how IMDA will consider workforce impact in merger assessments and whether tripartite partners will have a formal role and guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, how does the Government intend for IMDA to consider workforce impact as part of merger assessments, and can tripartite partners have a formal role in significant transactions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, will the Government develop clear guidelines, in consultation with MOM and NTUC, on collective agreement continuity, union recognition and representation where consolidations or structural separations result in workers moving to a new employing entity especially if only the property is transferred to a new entity under section 69A(3)(a)(ii), and the workers have to move as well?

sections.label: Media framework modernisation updates
sections.summary: The Bill modernises the media framework through section 61A intervention powers, expanded section 2 definitions, section 72A approval at 30%, and section 69A structural separation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, the services we rely on – our mobile plans, streaming platforms, online news and even everyday communication apps – are deeply interconnected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill modernises the media framework through several important updates: the new section 61A, which gives IMDA stronger and earlier intervention powers; expanded definitions in section 2 to capture modern, non-shareholding forms of influence; the new section 72A, which requires mandatory approval when an acquirer crosses the 30% ownership threshold; and the new section 69A, which empowers the Minister to order structural separation in serious cases of entrenched dominance.

sections.label: Section 72A acquisition scrutiny
sections.summary: Section 72A requires IMDA approval once a party crosses the 30% ownership threshold, preventing quiet large acquisitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Section 72A ensures that large acquisitions cannot take place quietly or without scrutiny, it requires IMDA's approval once a party crosses the 30% ownership threshold, thus preventing companies from using control over key digital or media resources to limit choice or raise barriers for others.

sections.label: IMDA regulatory toolkit strengthened
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens IMDA's regulatory toolkit through section 61A, broader section 2 definitions, section 72A approval, and section 69A structural separation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens IMDA’s regulatory toolkit through section 61A on early intervention, broader definitions under section 2, mandatory approval for acquisitions at the 30% threshold in section 72A, and the new section 69A on structural separation.

sections.label: Minister's structural separation power
sections.summary: Section 69A gives the Minister authority to order structural separation, a remedy the Senior Minister of State said would be used as a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Section 69A, which gives the Minister authority to order structural separation, is a powerful remedy – and I am glad that the Senior Minister of State had also raised this point and said that it would be a power that would be used as last resort.

sections.label: Bill's powers and three concerns
sections.summary: The speaker focuses on three areas: whether preventing excessive concentration of control facilitates new entry and jobs, whether new powers are exercised with clarity and predictability, and whether fairer market conditions benefit consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, by preventing harmful consolidation and ensuring fair access to essential resources, it helps create an open and competitive environment that innovation depends on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But clear guidance from IMDA will be important to ensure that these expanded powers truly support innovation rather than inadvertently discouraging it.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It shapes who they trust and also how we understand one another as a society.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do not intend to speak on every single clause in this Bill but I wish to focus on three specific areas: first, whether preventing excessive concentration of control will also help to facilitate new entrance and create jobs; second, whether the new powers will be exercised with sufficient clarity and predictability, so that Singapore remains trusted and investable; and third, whether fairer market conditions will translate to better outcomes for consumers.

sections.label: Upskilling and vibrant ecosystem
sections.summary: The question is whether preventing excessive concentration of control can translate into a more vibrant ecosystem where more players can enter, grow and hire.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But if Singaporeans were to upskill, they must also feel that the real opportunities exist at the end of their effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, the question is not really about whether this Bill prevents excessive concentration of control, but the question is whether preventing such concentration of control can translate into a more vibrant ecosystem where more players can enter, grow and hire.

sections.label: Risk to new and small players
sections.summary: The speaker asks IMDA how a framework designed to prevent unfair dominance will avoid unintentionally reducing vibrancy and entry that competition depends on.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Will the unintended consequences then be that new and small players find it harder to enter or scale?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, my question to IMDA is this: how will we ensure that a framework designed to prevent unfair dominance does not unintentionally reduce vibrancy and entry that competition depends on?

sections.label: Oversight of 30% acquisitions
sections.summary: The Bill closes a gap so that if any party, including a non-media company, seeks to acquire 30% or more of equity interest or voting power in a regulated person, IMDA would have oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It shows that Singapore is committed to fair and well-governed markets in the media industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand, for example, the Bill closes a gap that says that if any party, including a non-media company, seeks to acquire 30% or more of equity interest or voting power in a regulated person, IMDA would have oversight.

sections.label: Purpose of the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to prevent unfair dominance, regulate control and ensure important media resources are not used in ways that harm competition or the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: More precisely, it seeks to prevent unfair dominance, regulate control and ensure important media resources are not used in ways that harm competition or the public interest.

sections.label: Media competition and local content
sections.summary: Speaker hopes IMDA considers whether residents experience more choice, service quality and local content discoverability, and upholds three balances in the media framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A young person may consume a lot of media but encounter very little local content.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, when we assess whether market-level competition has improved, I hope IMDA would also consider whether residents actually experience more choice, better service quality and greater discoverability of local content.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is right that our regulatory framework keeps pace with the changes in the media landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But as we do so, we must uphold three balances carefully: first, preventing dominance and allowing new firms to enter; second, regulatory strength and investability; third, market competition and consumer trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Getting this right would help us to be a more open, vibrant, trusted and future-ready media ecosystem for Singapore.
